lines: You're up.
Good, 'cause I've been up since six and it's boring being the only one.
Morning. Roads are quiet.
Which either means it's a good day or everyone's waiting for something.
You look like you slept in your coat.
No, I'm not asking.
Afternoon. High street's rammed — everyone's got their phone out like it's free money.
Where've you been?
Don't answer that, I've got things to tell you.
There he is.
Night shift, yeah? Pays better. Costs more.
It's late. Which is fine, I'm not your mum.
Though she did ring me.
Right. Two days.
I'm not going to make it weird.
Here's what you missed.
Four days.
I rang you twice.
No, don't explain, honestly. You're here now.
Your corner's been stacking up like nobody owns it.
Which, for four days, nobody did.
Look who it is.
Sit down, I'll catch you up, and then we're not talking about it again.
How's the face?
Don't. I'm allowed one.
Right, that's the bad bit done.
Everyone gets one. Let's not make it a habit.
So. Word's out.
You did that with a crowbar and a bin bag and I'm not going to let you forget it.
You've gone quiet since you got money.
Classic.
Before you do anything — you're hot.
Properly hot. Everyone knows you were out last night.
Before anything else — go and pick your money up.
It's sat there embarrassing both of us.
Nothing's cooking. Which is a problem, because that means we're not earning.
Right — I've got one thing. Small thing. You want it?
You're here. Good.
Let's make the day worth something.
